title: Live GitHub admin token found in Baseten's public Docker image
plain: An autonomous security-testing agent (Strix), run without credentials or source code access against Baseten's public-facing infrastructure, discovered a public Harbor container registry project and pulled an image named baseten/baseten-app. Inside the image's build history metadata it found a live GitHub personal acces

angles.claim: Any vendor whose Docker images you pull should be audited for secrets in build history metadata, not just final image layers.
angles.audience: AI engineering leads who vet and integrate third-party AI infrastructure vendors
angles.rank_reason: Directly actionable check that changes what an engineering leader inspects before or after onboarding a vendor, grounded in the article's own remediation guidance.

angles.claim: A three-year-old credential still granting admin access shows that rotation on schedule, not just on incident, must be a governed control for vendor and internal tokens.
angles.audience: AI platform and security leads who set credential lifecycle policy
angles.rank_reason: Reaches the reader and changes policy, but is a narrower inference than the audit claim since the article documents discovery and remediation, not a rotation-cadence failure specifically.

angles.claim: Fast vendor response to a disclosed breach does not substitute for verifying that build pipelines never persisted secrets in the first place.
angles.audience: Directors deciding what to ask vendors about security posture
angles.rank_reason: Useful boardroom question but softer on decision-changing force since it restates the article's contrast between responsiveness and direct testing rather than adding a new obligation.
